1. Load borough Transport data (33 rows, no missing values) into a pandas Series; load the neighbor‐list into an adjacency dict for each borough.  
2. For every borough i, compute the spatial lag Lᵢ = mean(Transport_j) for all neighbors j in its list.  
   • All boroughs have at least one neighbor, so no lag value will be missing.  
3. Fit an initial city-wide OLS regression: Transportᵢ = α + β·Lᵢ + εᵢ.  
   • Save fitted values Ŷᵢ and residuals rᵢ = Transportᵢ – Ŷᵢ.  
4. Iterative-R masking correction (Lu, Chen & Kou, 2003):  
   a. Standardize residuals to zᵢ = rᵢ / σ, where σ is the residual std.  
   b. Flag any borough with |zᵢ| > 2.5 as a provisional outlier.  
   c. If at least one borough is flagged, temporarily remove it, re-estimate the regression on the remaining set, recompute residuals and z-scores, and repeat steps a–c until no new boroughs are flagged.  
   • Because Hillingdon itself might be removed in an early round, the procedure guards against its value distorting the model (masking).  
5. After convergence, place all removed boroughs back into the final model coefficients; compute Hillingdon’s final standardized residual z_Hill with those coefficients.  
6. Decision rule for Hillingdon:  
   • If |z_Hill| ≤ 2.5 ⇒ NOT AN OUTLIER.  
   • If z_Hill > 2.5 ⇒ OUTLIER – HIGH.  
   • If z_Hill < –2.5 ⇒ OUTLIER – LOW.  
7. Report only Hillingdon’s final z_Hill (a real number) and the corresponding classification in the required single-line format.  
8. Missing-value handling: Transport_value has 0 missing values; no imputation needed.

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from collections import defaultdict

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Load data
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
TRANSPORT_PATH = "chunks_csv/outlierr/2022_transport.csv"
ADJACENCY_PATH = "chunks_csv/borough_adjacency.csv"

df = pd.read_csv(TRANSPORT_PATH)              # columns: borough, Transport_value
adj = pd.read_csv(ADJACENCY_PATH)             # columns: borough, neighbor

df.set_index("borough", inplace=True)
transport_series = df["Transport_value"]

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Build an (undirected) adjacency dictionary
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
neighbors = defaultdict(set)
for _, row in adj.iterrows():
    b1, b2 = row["borough"], row["neighbor"]
    neighbors[b1].add(b2)
    neighbors[b2].add(b1)        # ensure the graph is undirected
neighbors = {k: list(v) for k, v in neighbors.items()}

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Helper to compute spatial lag (mean of neighbours *currently in sample*)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
def spatial_lag(values: pd.Series, active_mask: pd.Series) -> pd.Series:
    """Return Series of spatial lags for the boroughs whose active_mask == True."""
    lags = {}
    active_index = active_mask[active_mask].index
    for boro in active_index:
        # first try neighbours that are still in the active sample
        neighs_in_sample = [n for n in neighbors[boro] if active_mask.get(n, False)]
        if not neighs_in_sample:                     # if none left, fall back to full neighbours
            neighs_in_sample = neighbors[boro]
        # Corner-case: a (very unlikely) borough with absolutely no neighbours
        if not neighs_in_sample:
            lags[boro] = np.nan
            continue
        lags[boro] = values.loc[neighs_in_sample].mean()
    return pd.Series(lags)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Iterative-R masking-resistant procedure
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
in_sample = pd.Series(True, index=transport_series.index)
flagged_boroughs = set()
MAX_ITER = 20
CONVERGENCE = False

for _ in range(MAX_ITER):
    # spatial lags for the current sample
    lag_s = spatial_lag(transport_series, in_sample)

    # Assemble the regression design matrix
    y = transport_series.loc[in_sample.index[in_sample]]
    X = np.column_stack((np.ones(len(y)), lag_s.values))
    # Ordinary Least Squares
    coef, _, _, _ = np.linalg.lstsq(X, y.values, rcond=None)
    alpha, beta = coef
    y_hat = X @ coef
    resid = y.values - y_hat
    # Residual standard deviation with df = n - p  (p=2 here)
    sigma = resid.std(ddof=2)

    # Standardised residuals
    z_scores = resid / sigma
    # borough names aligned with z_scores
    boroughs_current = y.index
    newly_flagged = {b for b, z in zip(boroughs_current, z_scores) if abs(z) > 2.5 and b not in flagged_boroughs}

    if not newly_flagged:
        # nothing new was flagged ⇒ convergence
        CONVERGENCE = True
        break

    # remove newly flagged boroughs from the next round
    for b in newly_flagged:
        in_sample[b] = False
    flagged_boroughs.update(newly_flagged)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Final statistics for Hillingdon
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
#   • Use the final model coefficients (alpha, beta, sigma) from the converged iteration
#   • Compute Hillingdon's spatial lag from the *full* data (all neighbours present),
#     so that it is evaluated against an unbiased city-wide relationship
target = "Hillingdon"
lag_H = transport_series.loc[neighbors[target]].mean()
pred_H = alpha + beta * lag_H
resid_H = transport_series.loc[target] - pred_H
z_H = resid_H / sigma

# Classification
if abs(z_H) <= 2.5:
    verdict = "NOT AN OUTLIER"
elif z_H > 2.5:
    verdict = "OUTLIER - HIGH"
else:
    verdict = "OUTLIER - LOW"

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Required prints
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
data_points_used = int(in_sample.sum())          # number of boroughs retained in final regression

print(f"data_points_used = {data_points_used}")
print(f"FINAL ANSWER: {verdict} (z = {z_H})")
